text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria sets stiffer penalty for gas flaring by oil companies to cut down on pollution in the oil-producing areas, says Oil Minister Dan Etete.
- Central Bank to computerise its clearing system in a major overhaul of its operations, banking sources say.

- Foreign investors have redeemed external debts valued at $1.04 billion through a debt conversion programme instituted since 1988, Central Bank debt conversion manager E.O. Adesina tells a banking seminar in Abeokuta, southwestern Nigeria.

- Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi lists four-point Nigerian agenda as Nigeria resumes talks with Commonwealth team on human rights and democracy. They are lifting of its suspension from Commonwealth, end to threat of sanctions, support for its civil rule plan and dialogue at highest level
- Opposition lawyers Femi Falana and Gani Fawehinmi regain freedom after nearly a year in detention without trial, says state-owned News Agency of Nigeria.
- Nigeria says two Canadian security officers were denied visas to Nigeria because they were carrying weapons.

- A World Bank report still being compiled predicts that Nigeria's average annual economic growth for the non-oil sector could be 7.5 percent and could even catch up with Asian Tigers if military ruler General Sani Abacha's economic reforms are sustained next year and beyond.
- Exiled former foreign minister Bolaji Akinyemi, a member of Nigerian opposition abroad, eyes job of United Nations secretary general, say unnamed sources.
- Foreign minister Tom Ikimi accuses Canada of atrocities against Nigeria by funding opposition groups.
- Guiness Overseas Ltd converts its 1.6 billion naira debenture stock in Guiness Nigeria into equity holding, giving it a majority shareholding of 52 percent in the Nigerian firm.
